M_fixed: For a Keller map $F:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C^n$ ($\det JF\in\mathbb C^\times$) of geometric degree $d\ge2$, let $\mathrm{Mon}(F)\le S_d$ be the geometric monodromy group (Galois group of the Galois closure of $\mathbb C(x)/\mathbb C(F)$ acting on the $d$ embeddings). It is transitive, and by Campbell's theorem it is regular only if $d=1$. Let $\mathcal M$ be the set of transitive groups (up to permutation isomorphism) arising as $\mathrm{Mon}(F)$ for non-invertible Keller maps in some dimension; $\mathcal M$ contains $S_d$, $A_d$ (e.g. $d=6,12$ and the families of Kistner-Shaska 2608.02863) and imprimitive wreath-type groups (Fonollosa 2609.33491), and is closed under direct products in product action ($F\times G$). Is $\mathcal M$ exactly the set of non-regular transitive groups? Test case: does some primitive group not containing $A_d$ (e.g. $\mathrm{AGL}(1,p)$ for a prime $p\ge5$, or $\mathrm{PSL}(2,7)$ on 7 points) lie in $\mathcal M$? Equivalently, is every primitive member of $\mathcal M$ alternating or symmetric?
notes: Proposed decisive test case is already answered: Kistner-Shaska (2608.02863, in reviewer's own refs) prove geometric monodromy A_12 (Thm 5.5), A_6, A_N for k even (Thm 6.1), A_{2r-1} (Thm 6.5). W and why wrongly omit alternating groups. Full inverse problem is still open but no paper poses it and it is inverse-Galois-scale with no visible path. Fixed M uses a primitive non-A_d test.
